py: wǒ jīn tiān zài yī yuàn shàng bān
en: I'm working at the hospital today.
why: Time word, then 在 + place, then the verb. 在医院 cannot trail 上班 the way 'at the hospital' trails 'work' in English.

py: tā wǎn shang zài jiā kàn shǒu jī
en: He looks at his phone at home in the evening.
why: When comes before where, and both come before 看. 他看手机在家晚上 copies English order and is wrong.

zh: 医生明天上午在办公室见你。
py: yī shēng míng tiān shàng wǔ zài bàn gōng shì jiàn nǐ
en: The doctor will see you in the office tomorrow morning.
why: Subject, time, 在 + place, verb. The time may also open the sentence, but neither time nor place may follow 见你.

zh: 我们每个星期六在公园跑步。
py: wǒ men měi gè xīng qī liù zài gōng yuán pǎo bù
en: We jog in the park every Saturday.
why: The time phrase comes before the place phrase, and both sit ahead of the verb 跑步. Putting 在公园 last is the English habit.

zh: 我每天早上七点在楼下的公园锻炼身体。
py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang qī diǎn zài lóu xià de gōng yuán duàn liàn shēn tǐ
en: I exercise in the park downstairs at seven every morning.
why: Time first (even a long one), then the 在 + place phrase, then the verb and object. Nothing describing when or where may come after 身体.

py: wǒ men yī qǐ qù yī yuàn
en: We're going to the hospital together.
why: 一起 sits right before the verb after a plural subject. 我们去一起医院 follows English 'go together' and is wrong.

py: wǒ gēn péng you yī qǐ qù yī yuàn
en: I go to the hospital with friends.
why: The companion phrase 跟朋友一起 goes before 去, because who you are with is scene-setting. 我去医院跟朋友一起 is English order.

zh: 我想跟妈妈一起去体检。
py: wǒ xiǎng gēn mā ma yī qǐ qù tǐ jiǎn
en: I want to go for a check-up with my mum.
why: The modal 想 comes before 跟妈妈一起, which in turn comes before the main verb 去. Placing the companion after 体检 is wrong.

zh: 昨天我和同学一起玩手机游戏。
py: zuó tiān wǒ hé tóng xué yī qǐ wán shǒu jī yóu xì
en: Yesterday I played mobile games with my classmates.
why: Time, subject, then 和同学一起, then the verb. 和 works like 跟 here, and the companion cannot come after 手机游戏.

zh: 他常常跟爸爸一起去医院看奶奶。
py: tā cháng cháng gēn bà ba yī qǐ qù yī yuàn kàn nǎi nai
en: He often goes to the hospital with his dad to see his grandmother.
why: The adverb 常常 follows the subject, then 跟爸爸一起 comes before the whole verb phrase 去医院看奶奶. The companion cannot be tacked on at the end.

py: wǒ yòng shǒu jī kàn xīn wén
en: I read the news on my phone.
why: The tool, 用手机, comes before the main verb 看. 我看新闻用手机 is English order and is wrong.

py: tā zuò dì tiě qù yī yuàn
en: He goes to the hospital by subway.
why: You take the subway first and then arrive, so 坐地铁 comes before 去. The means cannot follow 去医院.

py: tā yòng zhōng wén fā duǎn xìn
en: She sends text messages in Chinese.
why: The language used is a means, so 用中文 goes before 发. 她发短信用中文 mirrors English and is wrong.

zh: 我每天骑自行车去上班。
py: wǒ měi tiān qí zì xíng chē qù shàng bān
en: I cycle to work every day.
why: Time word, then the means 骑自行车, then the main verb 去上班. The means cannot come after 上班.

zh: 他常常用手机上网查健康知识。
py: tā cháng cháng yòng shǒu jī shàng wǎng chá jiàn kāng zhī shi
en: He often goes online with his phone to look up health information.
why: 常常 follows the subject, 用手机 comes before the verbs it serves, and the verbs follow in the order they happen. The tool cannot be placed after 查健康知识.

py: wǒ yě xiǎng mǎi xīn shǒu jī
en: I want to buy a new phone too.
why: 也 follows the subject and comes before the modal 想. It cannot start the sentence or end it like English 'too'.

py: tā yǐ jīng zài yī yuàn le
en: He is already at the hospital.
why: 已经 goes after the subject and before the 在 + place phrase. 他在医院已经了 puts it in the wrong place.

py: dì di zuó tiān yī zhí tóu téng
en: My younger brother had a headache the whole time yesterday.
why: The time word comes first, then 一直 directly before the predicate 头疼. 一直 never opens the sentence.

py: wǒ men cháng cháng shàng wǎng mǎi yào
en: We often buy medicine online.
why: 常常 sits between the subject and the verb phrase. 我们上网买药常常 puts it last like English 'often'.

py: tā liù diǎn jiù qǐ chuáng le
en: She was already up at six.
why: The time word comes first and 就 follows it, right before the verb. 就六点她起床了 is wrong because 就 cannot open the sentence.

zh: 我昨天晚上十二点才睡觉。
py: wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shang shí èr diǎn cái shuì jiào
en: I didn't go to bed until twelve last night.
why: 才 comes right after the time word 十二点 and before the verb. Placing 才 at the end or before the time word is wrong.

py: yī shēng hái méi lái
en: The doctor hasn't arrived yet.
why: 还 goes after the subject and before 没. English 'yet' at the end does not carry over: 医生没来还 is wrong.

py: yé ye měi tiān dōu chī yào
en: Grandpa takes medicine every day.
why: Time word, then 都, then the verb. 都 cannot come before 爷爷 or after 吃药.

py: wǒ men yě dōu bù chōu yān
en: None of us smoke either.
why: The fixed stack is 也, 都, 不, verb. 我们都也不抽烟 and 我们不也都抽烟 break that order.

py: tā men yě dōu yǒu zhì néng shǒu jī
en: They all have smartphones too.
why: 也 comes before 都. 他们都也有智能手机 reverses them and is wrong.

py: wǒ yě bù zhī dào mì mǎ
en: I don't know the password either.
why: 也 comes before 不, so the answer is 也不. 我不也知道密码 puts them the wrong way round.

py: wǒ men dōu méi dài shǒu jī
en: None of us brought our phones.
why: 都 comes before 没 and means 'all, and all of them did not', so none of us brought a phone. 我们没都带手机 would mean only some did.

py: hái zi men dōu bù xǐ huan chī yào
en: None of the children like taking medicine.
why: 都不 means none. 不都 would only say 'not all of them', which does not match the cue 'none'.

zh: 我昨天买的手机很便宜。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de shǒu jī hěn pián yi
en: The phone I bought yesterday is cheap.
why: The whole clause 我昨天买 goes before 的 and the noun. The English order 'the phone I bought' cannot be used.

zh: 那个穿白衣服的医生是我叔叔。
py: nà ge chuān bái yī fu de yī shēng shì wǒ shū shu
en: The doctor in white is my uncle.
why: The description 穿白衣服 plus 的 goes before 医生. With 那个 it may stand before or after the description, but never after the noun.

py: zhè shì yī shēng gěi wǒ kāi de yào
en: This is the medicine the doctor prescribed for me.
why: The clause 医生给我开 goes before 的 and the noun 药. 这是药医生给我开的 copies English and is wrong.

py: wǒ xǐ huan nǐ fā de zhào piàn
en: I like the photos you sent.
why: 你发 modifies 照片, so it goes before 的 and the noun. 我喜欢照片你发的 puts the clause after the noun.

zh: 我想买一个很轻的新手机。
py: wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī gè hěn qīng de xīn shǒu jī
en: I want to buy a very light new phone.
why: The measure phrase 一个 comes first, then the description 很轻 + 的, then the noun. Nothing about the phone can follow 手机.

zh: 昨天帮我修电脑的那个人是小王的哥哥。
py: zuó tiān bāng wǒ xiū diàn nǎo de nà ge rén shì xiǎo wáng de gē ge
en: The person who fixed my computer yesterday is Xiao Wang's older brother.
why: The whole clause 昨天帮我修电脑 sits before 的 and 那个人. Chinese has no 'the person who...' order after the noun.

py: nǐ nǎ lǐ bù shū fu
en: Where do you feel unwell?
why: The question word stays where the answer would go: 我头不舒服 becomes 你哪里不舒服. It is not moved to the front.

py: nǐ shén me shí hou qù yī yuàn
en: When are you going to the hospital?
why: 什么时候 is a time word, so it sits where 明天 would: after the subject (or before it), ahead of the verb. It never goes last.

zh: 你想买什么颜色的手机？
py: nǐ xiǎng mǎi shén me yán sè de shǒu jī
en: What colour phone do you want to buy?
why: 什么颜色 describes 手机, so it stays in the modifier slot before 的 and the noun, just where 红色 would be.

py: nǐ zěn me qù yī yuàn
en: How do you get to the hospital?
why: 怎么 asks about the means, so it takes the manner slot before the verb. 你去医院怎么 is English-style and is wrong.

py: nǐ měi tiān shàng wǎng jǐ gè xiǎo shí
en: How many hours a day are you online?
why: The answer 三个小时 would follow the verb, so 几个小时 stays there. 几个小时你每天上网 fronts it, which is not allowed.

py: nǐ gēn shéi yī qǐ qù yī yuàn
en: Who are you going to the hospital with?
why: 谁 stays in the companion slot inside 跟…一起, before the verb. English moves 'who' to the front; Chinese does not.

py: zhè ge yào wǒ chī guo
en: I've taken this medicine.
why: A known object can be fronted as the topic, and the plain order 我吃过这个药 is also fine. The subject still comes right before the verb.

py: nà ge shǒu jī wǒ yě xiǎng mǎi
en: I want to buy that phone too.
why: After the fronted topic, 也 still follows the subject 我. 那个手机也我想买 is wrong because 也 cannot jump ahead of 我.

py: zhè ge yóu xì wǒ yě wán guo
en: I've played this game too.
why: The topic 这个游戏 opens the sentence; 也 stays after the subject and before 玩过.

py: duǎn xìn wǒ hái méi huí
en: I haven't replied to the text message yet.
why: The object 短信 can be fronted as a known topic, but 还没 still sits between the subject and the verb. Both topic-first and plain orders are correct.

py: zhè jiā yī yuàn wǒ yě qù guo
en: I've been to this hospital too.
why: A definite place can be fronted as the topic; the adverb 也 stays after 我. 这家医院也我去过 is wrong.

py: wǒ xiān liáng tǐ wēn zài chī yào
en: I'll take my temperature first, then take medicine.
why: 先 and 再 are adverbs: each goes after the subject and right before its verb phrase. The actions must follow their real order.

py: nǐ xiān chōng diàn zài wán yóu xì
en: Charge it first, then play the game.
why: 先 goes right before the first action and 再 before the second. 先你充电 would wrongly treat 先 as a sentence opener.

zh: 我们先挂号，再去看医生。
py: wǒ men xiān guà hào zài qù kàn yī shēng
en: We'll register first and then go to see the doctor.
why: 先 follows 我们 and precedes 挂号; 再 comes right before 去看医生. 再 cannot trail its verb or close the sentence.

py: tā xiān xǐ shǒu rán hòu zài chī fàn
en: He washes his hands first, and then eats.
why: 然后 may be added as a link, but 再 still stands directly before the second verb phrase 吃饭.

zh: 你先休息一下，然后我们再去医院。
py: nǐ xiān xiū xi yī xià rán hòu wǒ men zài qù yī yuàn
en: Rest for a bit first, and then we'll go to the hospital.
why: The second clause has its own subject 我们, and 再 follows that subject, not the first one. 然后 can sit before the subject.

zh: 我今天晚上在家看电视。
py: wǒ jīn tiān wǎn shang zài jiā kàn diàn shì
en: I'm watching TV at home tonight.
why: When comes before where, both before the verb. 在家今天晚上 puts the place ahead of the time, which is wrong.

zh: 小王每天早上在公园锻炼身体。
py: xiǎo wáng měi tiān zǎo shang zài gōng yuán duàn liàn shēn tǐ
en: Xiao Wang exercises in the park every morning.
why: The time phrase (large unit first) precedes 在 + place. The other orders put the place before the time.

py: wǒ men yě dōu bù hē jiǔ
en: None of us drink either.
why: The stack is always 也, 都, 不. The other options scramble that order.

q: 我们___是医生，只有小李是。
zh: 我们不都是医生，只有小李是。
py: wǒ men bù dōu shì yī shēng zhǐ yǒu xiǎo lǐ shì
en: Not all of us are doctors; only Xiao Li is.
why: 不都 means 'not all' and fits 'only Xiao Li is'. 都不 would mean none of us are doctors, which contradicts the second clause.

q: 明天我们___去医院，大家都想在家休息。
zh: 明天我们都不去医院，大家都想在家休息。
py: míng tiān wǒ men dōu bù qù yī yuàn dà jiā dōu xiǎng zài jiā xiū xi
en: Tomorrow none of us is going to the hospital; everyone wants to rest at home.
why: 'None of us' is 都不. 不都 would say only some of us go, which conflicts with everyone wanting to stay home.

q: 他十二点___睡觉，所以早上起不来。
zh: 他十二点才睡觉，所以早上起不来。
py: tā shí èr diǎn cái shuì jiào suǒ yǐ zǎo shang qǐ bù lái
en: He didn't go to bed until twelve, so he can't get up in the morning.
why: 才 marks 'as late as twelve', which explains why he can't get up. 就 would mean twelve was early, which does not fit the result clause.

q: 我六点___起床了，现在还很困。
zh: 我六点就起床了，现在还很困。
py: wǒ liù diǎn jiù qǐ chuáng le xiàn zài hái hěn kùn
en: I got up as early as six, and I'm still sleepy now.
why: 就 plus 了 shows six was early. 才 would mean late and cannot take 了 here.

py: wǒ men míng tiān yī qǐ qù yī yuàn
en: We're going to the hospital together tomorrow.
why: 一起 goes directly before the verb 去. 去一起 uses English order, and 在 cannot introduce a destination.

zh: 她每天晚上用手机看电影。
py: tā měi tiān wǎn shang yòng shǒu jī kàn diàn yǐng
en: Every evening she watches films on her phone.
why: The tool phrase is 用 + noun and goes before the main verb. 手机用 is not a Chinese phrase.

zh: 爸爸给我买的手机很好用。
py: bà ba gěi wǒ mǎi de shǒu jī hěn hǎo yòng
en: The phone my dad bought me is very easy to use.
why: The whole clause plus 的 must stand before 手机. Without 的 the clause is not a modifier, and the third option scrambles the clause.

py: shéi gěi nǐ dǎ diàn huà
en: Who is calling you?
why: The asker wants a person, and the question word sits in the subject slot where the answer would go. 什么 and 哪儿 ask about things and places.

py: zhè zhǒng yào wǒ yě chī guo
en: I've taken this medicine too.
why: After a fronted topic the adverb stays after the subject: 我也吃过. 也我 puts 也 ahead of the subject.

py: nǐ xiān chī fàn zài chī yào
en: Eat first, then take the medicine.
why: 先 marks the first action and 再 the second. 再 here would clash with the 再 already in the sentence, and 才 is a different adverb.

zh: 我们先去药店，再去医院。
py: wǒ men xiān qù yào diàn zài qù yī yuàn
en: We'll go to the pharmacy first and then to the hospital.
why: 再 pairs with 先 for 'then'. 先 twice makes no sense, and 也 would mean 'also' instead of 'then'.

py: wǒ tóu téng wǒ mèi mei yě tóu téng
en: I have a headache, and my younger sister has a headache too.
why: 'Too' is 也, placed after the subject. 还 would mean 'still' and 都 needs a plural subject.

task: Say he goes with his mother, using 跟…一起.
zh: 小王跟妈妈一起去医院。
py: xiǎo wáng gēn mā ma yī qǐ qù yī yuàn
en: Xiao Wang goes to the hospital with his mum.
why: The companion phrase goes before the verb 去. Adding 跟妈妈一起 after 医院 is English order.

src_py: wǒ men bù hē kā fēi
task: Say none of us drink coffee either, using 也 and 都.
py: wǒ men yě dōu bù hē kā fēi
en: None of us drink coffee either.
why: The stack is 也, 都, 不, then the verb. 都不 gives 'none', while 不都 would only mean 'not all'.

task: Say you go there by bike, using 骑自行车.
py: wǒ qí zì xíng chē qù gōng sī
en: I ride my bike to the office.
why: The means goes before the main verb: you get on the bike, then you go.

task: Say 'first take the medicine, then go to sleep' with 先…再.
py: nǐ xiān chī yào zài shuì jiào
en: Take your medicine first, then go to sleep.
why: 先 and 再 each sit directly before their own verb, after the subject. 先 cannot open the sentence.

src_py: wǒ mǎi le nà bù shǒu jī
task: Say it is the one your older brother recommended, using 的.
zh: 我买了哥哥推荐的那部手机。
py: wǒ mǎi le gē ge tuī jiàn de nà bù shǒu jī
en: I bought the phone my older brother recommended.
why: The clause 哥哥推荐 plus 的 goes before the noun phrase. Chinese cannot say 那部手机哥哥推荐的 after the noun.

src_py: tā zài yào diàn mǎi yào
task: Ask where he buys medicine, using 哪儿.
py: tā zài nǎ r mǎi yào
en: Where does he buy medicine?
why: 哪儿 replaces 药店 in the same slot, 在 + place before the verb. It is not moved to the front, and no 吗 is added.

src_py: wǒ kàn guo zhè ge shì pín
task: Put 这个视频 first as the topic.
py: zhè ge shì pín wǒ kàn guo
en: I've seen this video.

task: Say he was already up at five, using 就 and 了.
py: tā wǔ diǎn jiù qǐ chuáng le
en: He was already up at five.
why: 就 goes right after the time word and before the verb, and 了 closes the sentence. 就 cannot come before 他.

src_py: tā zài wǎng shàng mǎi yào
task: Say you buy medicine online too, using 也.
py: wǒ yě zài wǎng shàng mǎi yào

task: Say you write with your left hand, using 用左手.
py: wǒ yòng zuǒ shǒu xiě zì
en: I write with my left hand.
why: The tool phrase 用左手 comes before the verb 写. 我写字用左手 mirrors English and is wrong.

s_py: wǒ qù yī yuàn míng tiān
py: wǒ míng tiān qù yī yuàn
en: I'm going to the hospital tomorrow.
why: A time word cannot end the sentence. It belongs after the subject, before the verb.

s_py: wǒ kàn shǒu jī zài chuáng shàng
py: wǒ zài chuáng shàng kàn shǒu jī

s_py: wǒ qù yī yuàn gēn mā ma yī qǐ
py: wǒ gēn mā ma yī qǐ qù yī yuàn

s_py: wǒ men qù yī qǐ ba

s_py: tā diàn nǎo yòng zuò zuò yè

s_py: yě wǒ xǐ huan zhè ge shǒu jī
py: wǒ yě xǐ huan zhè ge shǒu jī
en: I like this phone too.

s_py: wǒ men qù yī yuàn dōu
py: wǒ men dōu qù yī yuàn
en: We all go to the hospital.
why: 都 goes before the verb, after the subject. It never ends the sentence like English 'all'.

s_py: tā men dōu yě yǒu shǒu jī
py: tā men yě dōu yǒu shǒu jī
en: They all have phones too.
why: In stacked adverbs 也 comes before 都. 都也 reverses them.

s_py: wǒ xǐ huan shǒu jī nǐ mǎi de
py: wǒ xǐ huan nǐ mǎi de shǒu jī
en: I like the phone you bought.

s_py: wǒ kàn dào le rén chuān bái yī fu de

s_py: xiān wǒ xǐ zǎo zài shuì jiào
py: wǒ xiān xǐ zǎo zài shuì jiào
en: I'll take a shower first, then go to sleep.

py: zhè ge ruǎn jiàn wǒ yě yòng guo
en: I've used this software too.

py: hái zi men bù dōu xǐ huan chī táng
en: Not all children like sweets.
why: 不都 is correct for 'not all'; it differs from 都不 ('none'). The order depends on the meaning.

s: 我不想跟他一起去医院。
zh: 我不想跟他一起去医院。
py: wǒ bù xiǎng gēn tā yī qǐ qù yī yuàn
en: I don't want to go to the hospital with him.
why: Correct: 不想 comes before the whole 跟他一起 phrase, which stays ahead of the main verb 去.

s: 我上个月买的电脑很好用。
zh: 我上个月买的电脑很好用。
py: wǒ shàng gè yuè mǎi de diàn nǎo hěn hǎo yòng
en: The computer I bought last month is very easy to use.
why: Correct: the clause 我上个月买 sits before 的 and the noun 电脑, with the time inside the clause.

py: tā shí yī diǎn cái huí jiā
en: He didn't get home until eleven.
why: Correct: 才 follows the time word and precedes the verb, with no 了 afterwards.

s: 你先吃点儿东西，然后再吃药。
zh: 你先吃点儿东西，然后再吃药。
py: nǐ xiān chī diǎn r dōng xi rán hòu zài chī yào
en: Eat something first, and then take the medicine.
why: Correct: 先 and 再 each sit directly before their own verb, and 然后 may come between the clauses.

py: qǐng nǐ màn màn de shuō
en: Please speak slowly.
why: Correct: the manner phrase 慢慢地 comes before the verb 说, as every manner word does.

s: 小王每个星期六在公园跑步。
zh: 小王每个星期六在公园跑步。
py: xiǎo wáng měi gè xīng qī liù zài gōng yuán pǎo bù
en: Xiao Wang jogs in the park every Saturday.
why: Correct: the time phrase comes before 在公园, and both come before 跑步.

py: nǐ shén me shí hou mǎi de shǒu jī
en: When did you buy your phone?
why: Correct: 什么时候 stays in the time slot before the verb. There is no fronting and no 吗.

py: wǒ men dōu bù zhī dào mì mǎ
en: None of us know the password.
why: Correct: 都 comes before 不, giving 'none of us'.

s: 我也跟哥哥一起去过医院。
zh: 我也跟哥哥一起去过医院。
py: wǒ yě gēn gē ge yī qǐ qù guo yī yuàn
en: I've also been to the hospital with my older brother.
why: Correct: 也 follows the subject and comes before the whole phrase 跟哥哥一起.

py: diàn nǎo wǒ yǐ jīng xiū hǎo le
en: I've already fixed the computer.
why: Correct: 电脑 is a known topic, and 已经 stays after the subject 我 and before the verb.
